subject: Backup purge scheduling and emergency restore workflow — DPA alignment
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medicore.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal - MedicoRe <legal@medicore.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Backup purge schedule & emergency restore window — DPA implications

Team,

Thanks for taking this meeting last week. Following up with the items Legal asked us to confirm for the DPA:

- MedicoRe regulatory mandate requires up to 6 years of raw transaction logs for audit; our current internal purge schedule for overnight backups is 90 days. Can you confirm whether Redwood can support a longer tombstone window for this account?
- We need a documented emergency restore workflow (RTO target 48 hours) and a responsibility matrix for who initiates restores vs. who handles retention holds.
- Please confirm the list of subprocessors who may hold backups (storage providers, managed snapshots). Legal also wants confirmation on cross-border transfers for backups.

Attachments: backup_retention_matrix.xlsx (what we have on our side)

We appreciate an action plan with dates so Legal can review the redlines.

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Infrastructure Ops, MedicoRe

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medicore.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Legal - MedicoRe <legal@medicore.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Backup purge schedule & emergency restore window — DPA implications

Samir — thanks for the clear summary. High-level answers and proposed approach below; I like to align on the plan before Legal signs off.

1) Retention carveout: Redwood can offer a tombstone hold that prevents permanent deletion for a configurable carveout (we call this a "preservation hold"). We typically provide preservation holds in 30/90/365-day slices; for regulatory needs we can negotiate an extended preservation retention up to 6 years as an addendum to the DPA. This requires an ops flag and a billing adjustment.

2) Emergency restore workflow: We propose a documented runbook (attached: restore-playbook_v1.md) with the following SLA: initial restore staging within 24 hours, full RTO target 48 hours for snapshot-level restores for committed customers on dedicated capacity. For hosted accounts we offer 72 hours for archived restores.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: Karthik will enumerate the subprocessor list and indicate which ones may have snapshot access. Cross-border transfer controls are available (customer may restrict locations).

Immediate asks:
- Karthik: can you confirm which storage providers would be in-scope and whether we can commit to a 6-year preservation hold without additional encryption segmentation?
- Marcus: ops question on cost/space implications and whether we can support the preservation hold with our existing snapshot lifecycle or if we need a segmented cold archive.

I also attach a draft redline to the DPA (DPA_redline_v3.pdf) for Legal to review.

Thanks — I will coordinate a timeline once we have the technical confirmation.

Best,

Irene Choi
Sr. Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@medicore.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Legal - MedicoRe <legal@medicore.com>, Nadia Voronova <nadia@cypress-consulting.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Backup purge schedule & emergency restore window — DPA implications

Irene / Samir,

Quick technical notes (summary of subprocessor and transfer impact):

- Subprocessors: primary backup storage is S3-compatible block store provided by a regional partner (us-west-2), secondary cold archive is on an encrypted object store run by CloudTape Inc. Both are contractually bound as subprocessors. I list: CloudTape (cold archive), NimbusStore (hot snapshots), and GeoVault (replication).
- Cross-border transfers: for the MedicoRe "us" footprint we can restrict backups to us-west-2. For chosen archive tiers we do replicate to a second US region; no EU transfers unless customer requests cross-border replication.
- Implementation constraints: to guarantee a non-destructive 6-year preservation without impacting other tenants we recommend a segmented cold-archive bucket per customer with separate KMS key. That avoids requiring a global data carveout and simplifies deletion proofs.

Proposed timeline:
- By 2028-03-09: Ops spike to confirm storage sizing and cost delta for a per-customer cold archive.
- By 2028-03-16: Deliver final subprocessor list and updated DPA paragraph for preservation hold (Karthik / Legal).
- By 2028-03-23: Ops ready to accept preservation holds and test restore-playbook for a staged snapshot.

On the preservation semantics: we can support a tombstone hold that prevents irreversible purge. However, if Legal requires guaranteed on-site encryption separation (HSM/KMS with unique keys) we will need an enterprise addendum.

On quoting Samir:
> "Please confirm whether Redwood can support a longer tombstone window for this account?"

Answer: Yes, via per-customer cold archive + preservation hold; expect additional cost.

-Karthik
Senior Product Manager, Platform

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medicore.com>, Legal - MedicoRe <legal@medicore.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Nadia Voronova <nadia@cypress-consulting.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Mar 2028 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Backup purge schedule & emergency restore window — DPA implications

Samir / Legal team — consolidating and next steps below.

Decisions & commitments:
- Redwood will provision a customer-segmented cold archive for MedicoRe and enable a preservation hold that prevents purge for up to 6 years (requires addendum).
- Restore SLA commitment: 48 hours for staged snapshot restores (covered in the addendum for dedicated accounts); hosted restores documented at 72 hours.
- Subprocessors: NimbusStore, CloudTape, GeoVault (full contract names and addresses will be provided to Legal by 2028-03-16).
- Cross-border transfers: backups will be restricted to US regions by default; cross-border replication will require explicit customer opt-in and associated redlines.

Action items & dates:
- 2028-03-09: Ops sizing and cost delta (Marcus Lin) — will include expected monthly storage + retrieval cost.
- 2028-03-16: Final subprocessor manifest + DPA paragraph for preservation hold (Karthik Iyer + Redwood Legal).
- 2028-03-23: Dry-run of restore-playbook and evidence package for Legal (Irene / Ops).
- 2028-03-30: Target for executed DPA addendum (DocuSign link to follow).

Attachments: DPA_redline_v3.pdf, restore-playbook_v1.md, backup_retention_matrix.xlsx

If Legal has any required language about KMS separation or HSM-backed keys, flag that immediately — that will push the timeline and require procurement/engineering involvement.

Thanks everyone — I like to keep the meeting cadence weekly until the addendum is signed.

Best regards,

Irene Choi
Sr. Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--
References: INFRA-1293 (preservation-holds), DocuSign draft: https://docusign.net/ML7F88
